messages:
ops-oncall: alert: reserved-usw2 pool at 100% alloc, fair-share eviction triggered for low-priority jobs :warning:
eng-runtime: seeing a bunch of 429s from dedicated endpoints in us-west-2, backlog queue length jumped to ~40
infra-sre: confirmed. Admission controller logs show: ```admission_controller: pool=reserved-usw2 total_gpus=128 allocated=128 queued=41 evicted=9 policy=fair_share threshold=0.95```
product-ops: are these evictions affecting SLA customers?
cust-success: multiple customers pinged saying requests are timing out / getting rate limited. One enterprise customer (acme-inc) reported degraded throughput.
sales-lead: flagging ACME — they have a Dedicated SLA. We need a quick mitigation.
eng-runtime: quick mitigation options: (1) enable burst capacity (reserve burst GPUs) to absorb queued work; (2) temporarily bump ACME's fair-share weight to avoid eviction; (3) divert lower-priority jobs to hosted variants. Each has tradeoffs.
ops-oncall: what's the fastest?
eng-runtime: bumping weight for a specific customer is a config flip, relatively fast (~5-10m) but risks starving others. Enabling burst requires spinning up instances in same AZ — ~12-18m and costs extra. Diverting to hosted requires routing change + customer consent.
infra-sre: autoscaler attempted a scale-up at 1768504800 but failed due to AZ quota exhausted: `InsufficientCapacity: no more p4d in us-west-2a` — so burst won't come up in same AZ. Can spin in other AZs but KV-cache locality and latency impacts.
product-ops: propose: immediate temporary weight bump for ACME + notify them; follow-up: open cloud quota request and spin cross-AZ burners; medium-term: review capacity placement policies.
billing-bot: note: enabling cross-AZ burst will incur on-demand GPU spend, estimated +$22k/day if sustained.
ops-oncall: eng-runtime, please apply weight bump for ACME and add a 30m TTL. Notify cust-success when done.
eng-runtime: doing the weight bump now -> `PATCH /config/pools/reserved-usw2/fairshare` payload applied. Rolling in 30s.
deploy-bot: config-deploy succeeded: `deploy_id=deploy-3421` by eng-runtime at 1768504989
eng-runtime: ACME weight bumped, monitoring for evictions.
infra-sre: eviction rate dropped from 9->2 in last 5m, queue length down to 18. Latency for ACME looks stable.
cust-success: notified ACME: "We've temporarily prioritized your workloads while we increase capacity; we'll follow up with timeline." They acknowledged. :thumbsup:
ops-oncall: immediate customer impact mitigated. Next steps: (1) open cloud quota request for p4d in us-west-2a (infra-sre) (2) add cross-AZ fallback to admission controller to allow warm relocation (eng-runtime) (3) review fair-share defaults to reduce broad evictions (product-ops)
infra-sre: opened quota ticket with cloud provider (#CP-1129). Also starting cross-AZ warm up in us-west-2b/c — starting warm instances now but will need cache warmup time (~10-20m).
eng-runtime: will add a small admission-controller change: allow best-effort routing across AZs when reserved pool saturated, controlled by feature flag `cross_az_fallback` (will gate until QA).
product-ops: create post-incident note and customer comms draft. We should call out the tradeoff between latency and availability.
sales-lead: we need a billing adjustment discussion for ACME — they used burst capacity and we prioritized them. Will follow up with finance.
billing-bot: recorded usage spike for ACME and cluster-wide on-demand GPU spend. Billing ticket created (#BILL-879).
ops-oncall: timeline: current state "stabilized but degraded". Reopen if evictions > 3/min or queue > 50. Last check in 10m.
eng-runtime: adding trace logs to correlate per-customer evictions to request patterns. Will post a small extract if more anomalies show up.
infra-sre: cross-AZ warm nodes reporting healthy, but KV-sync lag ~2s — expect slight QoS jitter for moved sessions.
cust-success: ACME asked for a short RCA for their CSM — flagged to product-ops.
ops-oncall: thanks team. tagging this thread for postmortem. :white_check_mark:"
